biography: Claudiomiro Pacheco, a name whispered with respect (and sometimes frustration) in the Brazilian Uno Classic B circuit, hails from the dusty backroads of Minas Gerais. His racing journey began, not in a karting school, but behind the wheel of his grandfather's beat-up Fiat 147, delivering produce to the local markets. It was there, navigating treacherous dirt tracks and outmaneuvering stray dogs, that he honed his innate car control. He entered the Uno Classic B scene with a borrowed car and a burning desire. One defining moment early in his career came at Interlagos, where, despite starting last, he meticulously picked off competitors one by one, showcasing his defensive prowess and earning a surprise podium. Now in his early thirties, Pacheco is considered to be at his career peak, a seasoned veteran who continues to defy expectations in his trusty Uno Classic B.
drivingStyle: Pacheco is a master of defensive driving. He's not the flashiest driver on the grid, but he's notoriously difficult to overtake. He prefers a late-braking style, positioning his car perfectly to block any potential overtaking attempts. Tire management is a key strength; he nurses his tires throughout the race, often gaining an advantage in the closing laps when others are struggling for grip. Under pressure, he remains remarkably calm, rarely making mistakes and forcing his rivals to take unnecessary risks.

rivalries.name: Ricardo 'The Rocket' Albuquerque
rivalries.reason: A constant battle for track position, fueled by Albuquerque's aggressive overtaking style clashing with Pacheco's staunch defense.

rivalries.name: Isabela 'Ice Queen' Fonseca
rivalries.reason: A strategic rivalry; Fonseca often uses mind games and calculated risks that Pacheco finds frustrating, leading to on-track clashes.

rivalries.name: Joao 'The Joker' Carvalho
rivalries.reason: Carvalho's unpredictable driving and tendency for late-race heroics has often cost Pacheco valuable points and podium finishes.

quirks: Always wears the same faded São Paulo FC jersey under his racing suit.
Sharpens his pencils meticulously before each race, claiming it helps him focus.
Listens to a specific obscure Brazilian folk song on repeat during the formation lap.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest, it's about being the smartest. And sometimes, the smartest thing to do is to make sure nobody gets past you."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Minas Gerais State Championship after a season-long battle with Ricardo Albuquerque, solidifying his reputation as a defensive master.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2019 Rio Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential national title.
